# GitHub Copilot Instructions for vue-qs

## Project Overview

vue-qs is a type-safe search params state manager for Vue 3, and a port of
[nuqs](https://nuqs.dev) (React). Its parsers, options and behaviour follow nuqs.
Its surface follows Vue idioms: writable refs, reactive objects, `v-model`, plugin and
provide/inject.

When adding or changing a feature, check how nuqs implements it first, and keep the
same names and semantics unless Vue requires a different shape.

## Source Layout

| Path                                                           | Responsibility                                                      |
| -------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `src/parsers.ts`                                               | `createParser`, `createMultiParser` and built-in `parseAs*` parsers |
| `src/options.ts`                                               | `Options`, `throttle`, `debounce`, option resolution                |
| `src/composables/use-query-state.ts`                           | `useQueryState` (writable ref + `.set()`)                           |
| `src/composables/use-query-states.ts`                          | `useQueryStates` (reactive object + `$set`)                         |
| `src/lib/key-state.ts`                                         | Binds one URL key to reactive state (shared by both composables)    |
| `src/lib/queue.ts`                                             | Update queue: batching, throttle, debounce                          |
| `src/lib/runtime.ts`                                           | Per-adapter queue and sync emitter                                  |
| `src/adapters/*`                                               | Adapter interface, plugin/context, history, vue-router, testing     |
| `src/serializer.ts`, `src/loader.ts`, `src/standard-schema.ts` | Server utilities                                                    |
| `src/index.ts`, `src/server.ts`                                | Public entry points                                                 |

Package entry points: `vue-qs`, `vue-qs/server` (no Vue import), `vue-qs/adapters/history`,
`vue-qs/adapters/vue-router`, `vue-qs/adapters/testing`. Adapters are only exported from
their subpaths. `vue-router` must only be imported by `src/adapters/vue-router.ts`.

## Public API Names

- Composables: `useQueryState`, `useQueryStates`
- Plugin/context: `createVueQs`, `provideQueryAdapter`, `useQueryAdapter`, `VueQsAdapter`
- Adapters: `createHistoryAdapter`, `createVueRouterAdapter`, `createTestingAdapter`, `createAdapter`
- Parsers: `parseAs*`, `createParser`, `createMultiParser`, `.withDefault()`, `.withOptions()`
- Options: `history`, `scroll`, `shallow`, `clearOnDefault`, `limitUrlUpdates`, `throttle()`, `debounce()`
- Server: `createLoader`, `createSerializer`, `createStandardSchemaV1`, `inferParserType`

The 0.1.x API (`queryRef`, `queryReactive`, `*Codec`, `createVueQsPlugin`,
`historyStrategy`, `shouldOmitDefault`) has been removed. Never reintroduce it.

## Code Quality Standards

- Run `bun run lint`, `bun run typecheck`, `bun run test` and `bun run build` before committing
- Use `@/` alias imports in `src/` (tests may import local helpers relatively)
- Use kebab-case file names
- Explicit return types on exported functions; avoid `any`
- JSDoc with an `@example` on every public API; mark internals with `@internal`
- Prefer `debug()` from `src/lib/debug.ts` (enabled with `localStorage.debug = 'vue-qs'`)
  over console logging; use `warn()` only for actionable problems

## Testing

- Vitest + happy-dom; tests live in `tests/` (`unit`, `composables`, `adapters`)
- Use the testing adapter for composable tests, real happy-dom History for the history
  adapter, and `createMemoryHistory` for the Vue Router adapter
- Type-level tests go in `tests/types.test-d.ts` (`expectTypeOf`, run by `vitest --typecheck`)

## Documentation

- Update `README.md` and `docs/guide/*` together with code changes
- The API reference (`docs/api`) is generated by TypeDoc at build time and not committed
- Check the docs build (dead links) with `bun run docs:build`

## Git

- Conventional Commits (`feat:`, `fix:`, `docs:`, `chore:`…), `!` for breaking changes
- One commit per pull request; squash-merge
- Branches are named `<issue-number>-<short-slug>`
